title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 142
paragraphs: Of these Ionians, the Milesians were safe from danger because of their treaty. The islanders also had nothing to fear, since the Phoenicians were not yet Persian subjects, and the Persians themselves were not a seafaring people. The Ionians of the mainland had split from the others for one reason only: the Greek race as a whole was weak at that time, and the Ionians were by far the weakest and least significant part of it. Apart from Athens, no Ionian city of any importance existed. The Athenians and most other Ionians were ashamed of the name and did not want to be called Ionian. Even now, most of them seem to regard the name as a reproach. But the twelve Asiatic cities were proud of the name. They established a sanctuary called the Panionion exclusively for themselves and voted to exclude all other Ionians from it—though no one else actually asked to be admitted, except the people of Smyrna.
